questions.q: What is a SQL Server Maintenance Plan, under the hood?
options: A feature exclusive to Azure SQL Database
A stored procedure library with no scheduling capability
An SSIS package, built through an SSMS wizard, that generates a SQL Server Agent job
A standalone executable unrelated to SQL Server Agent
questions.explain: Maintenance Plans are SSIS packages created via the Maintenance Plan Wizard, and they run on a schedule as a SQL Server Agent job.

questions.q: Which real T-SQL statement does the Wizard's "Check Database Integrity" task actually run?
options: ALTER INDEX REBUILD
UPDATE STATISTICS
DBCC CHECKDB
BACKUP DATABASE
questions.explain: Check Database Integrity wraps DBCC CHECKDB, which detects corruption.

questions.q: What's the difference between the Wizard's Rebuild Index and Reorganize Index tasks?
options: Rebuild Index only works on Azure SQL Database
They are identical and interchangeable
Reorganize Index only works on statistics, not indexes
Rebuild Index runs ALTER INDEX REBUILD (heavier); Reorganize Index runs ALTER INDEX REORGANIZE (lighter, in-place)
questions.explain: Rebuild Index drops and rebuilds the index (heavier); Reorganize Index defragments in place with a lighter footprint.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what real limitation does the Maintenance Plan Wizard have that motivates Ola Hallengren's scripts (covered later in this chapter)?
options: It only works in Azure SQL Database, not on-prem
Its per-database, one-size-fits-all task configuration doesn't scale well once an instance has many databases with different sizes/fragmentation patterns
It cannot be scheduled — it must be run manually every time
It cannot run DBCC CHECKDB at all
questions.explain: Maintenance Plans are functional but the wizard-driven, per-database configuration doesn't scale cleanly across many varied databases, which is the gap Ola Hallengren's parameterized scripts fill.

questions.q: What does a completed Maintenance Plan's task list ultimately become?
options: A set of Always Encrypted column definitions
Entries in the Windows Task Scheduler only, with no SQL Server involvement
A single stored procedure with no scheduling
Steps in an underlying SQL Server Agent job
questions.explain: Each task in the plan becomes a step (or linked sub-plan) inside a real Agent job, editable like any other job.
